key_insight: The paper shows that memory retrieval for LLM agents should not only ask "what is relevant?" but also "should this memory be trusted?". By decoupling confidence from consistency and using three complementary signals, the controller can better decide when to use or ignore conflicting memories.
problem_solved: It addresses the failure of standard RAG-based memory systems that blindly inject retrieved memories, especially when the memory store contains conflicting or contradictory information. This can amplify hallucinations and make agents less reliable.
method: Introduces an interpretable memory decision controller that evaluates retrieved memories before they are injected into the LLM context.
Uses three-signal complementarity to separate confidence from consistency, helping detect when a memory is plausible but contradictory.
Makes the memory-use decision explicit and explainable, improving robustness under conflicting-memory scenarios.
impact: This matters because LLM agents increasingly rely on long-term memory, and incorrect memory usage can severely degrade performance. The approach gives practitioners a clearer, safer way to manage memory injection and reduce hallucination risk in agentic systems.
visual_elements: Flow diagram showing retrieval -> memory evaluation -> trust/ignore decision -> generation
Side-by-side comparison chart of standard RAG vs. the proposed controller under conflicting memories
Three-signal radar or triad icon illustrating complementarity between signals
Bar chart showing hallucination rate reduction when conflicting memories are filtered
paper_title: An Interpretable Memory Decision Controller for LLM Agents Based on Three-Signal Complementarity: Decoupling Confidence and Consistency
paper_authors: Yiming Zhang, Jinghong Zhang, Haoran Zhao, Yiren Ma, Chunlei Zhao
